obligor_name: Catholic Health Services of Long Island

moodys.citation_text: No Moody's identified for CHSLI. S&P and Fitch are active raters.

sp.citation_text: S&P holds CHSLI at 'A-' per 2024 outlook revision article — 'S&P said it could lower Catholic Health's credit rating from "A-"'. Implies A- in effect throughout window.

fitch.citation_text: Fitch affirmed BBB+ historically. June 2024 article notes Fitch downgraded financial outlook to negative — implies BBB+ still in effect with outlook revised in window.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: BBB+ affirmed; outlook revised stable -> negative
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Catholic Health's cash flow has deteriorated and it has been relying on two of its hospitals to offset the system's losses; thin margins; layoffs of 1% of 17,000-member workforce announced May 2024.
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: 'In June, credit ratings agency Fitch downgraded the health system's financial outlook to negative, noting that Catholic Health's cash flow has deteriorated.'

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: A- affirmed; outlook revised stable -> negative
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Growing operating losses through 2nd quarter; projected loss this fiscal year; expenses rising; payer mix shifting toward lower reimbursing plans; federal funding erosion under new administration.
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: S&P 'revised Catholic Health Services of Long Island's outlook from stable to negative, after operating losses continued to grow at the six-hospital system'. NOTE: Article context suggests action occurred in 2025; specific date not surfaced — may straddle window end.

sp.citation_text: A- with negative outlook (date of action uncertain — may be Q1 or Q2 2025).

fitch.citation_text: Fitch BBB+ negative as of June 2024.

outcome_class_rationale: Two outlook revisions to negative (Fitch June 2024, S&P Spring 2025) with no actual rating change during window. NOT a fallen angel — CHSLI remained IG (A-/BBB+). NOT a successor entity to Caritas Christi (that is a separate Boston-area Catholic system that became Steward Health Care). CHSLI is a 6-hospital Long Island system distinct from the Buffalo Catholic Health System.
